items.title: Good News about Bad News: Gamified Inoculation Boosts Confidence and Cognitive Immunity Against Fake News

judge.evidence_empirical: "Using a 2 (treatment vs. control) × 2 (pre vs. post) mixed design (N = 196) we measure participants’ ability to spot misinformation techniques"

judge.reason: O artigo trata de um jogo de inoculação (Bad News) contra desinformação, enquadrando-se no tema. O estudo é empírico, com delineamento experimental misto com grupo controle. O achado extraído é plenamente sustentado pelo resumo, que relata melhora na identificação de técnicas e aumento de confiança.

items.title: Prebunking interventions based on the psychological theory of "inoculation" can reduce susceptibility to misinformation across cultures

judge.evidence_topic: online “fake news” game, Bad News, can confer psychological resistance against common online misinformation strategies (e.g., conspiracy theories, manipulating emotions, political polarization) across different cultures

items.title: Long-term effectiveness of inoculation against misinformation: Three longitudinal experiments

judge.evidence_empirical: Using 3 longitudinal experiments (2 preregistered), we tested the effectiveness of Bad News, a real-world intervention in which participants develop resistance against misinformation through exposure to weakened doses of misinformation techniques. In 3 experiments (NExp1 = 151, NExp2 = 194, NExp3 = 170), participants played either Bad News (inoculation group) or Tetris (gamified control group) and rated the reliability of news headlines...
judge.evidence_topic: Bad News, a real-world intervention in which participants develop resistance against misinformation through exposure to weakened doses of misinformation techniques.
judge.reason: O resumo sustenta integralmente o achado extraído, relatando estabilidade por pelo menos 3 meses no Experimento 1 e decaimento significativo em 2 meses no Experimento 2.

items.title: Disentangling Item and Testing Effects in Inoculation Research on Online Misinformation: Solomon Revisited

judge.evidence_empirical: We investigate both item and testing effects in two online studies (total N = 2,159) using the Bad News game.
judge.evidence_topic: a widely adopted online “fake news” inoculation game, Bad News
judge.reason: O resumo trata do jogo de inoculação Bad News, um jogo digital contra desinformação, testado em dois estudos online com dados próprios, exatamente o tipo de intervenção e delineamento empírico solicitado.

items.title: Technique-based inoculation against real-world misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: two separate experiments (total n = 2188; convenience sample recruited via the Bad News online game platform)
judge.evidence_topic: technique-based inoculation... recruited via the Bad News online game platform
judge.reason: O achado informa que jogar 15 minutos confere resistência a desinformação real que usa as técnicas inoculadas, com proteção cruzada menor. O resumo confirma ambos: 'playing a 15 min game confers psychological resistance against real-world misinformation that makes use of manipulation techniques against which people were inoculated (Cohen's d = 0.37...)' e 'cross-protection is achieved but at a reduced effect size (d = 0.10...)'.

items.title: Game-based inoculation versus graphic-based inoculation to combat misinformation: a randomized controlled trial

judge.reason: O achado principal corresponde exatamente ao que o resumo relata: 'Game-based inoculation was more effective than graphic-based inoculation in terms of misinformation perceived credibility, and the intervention effects were stable after 2 weeks.'

items.title: Feedback exercises boost discernment of misinformation for gamified inoculation interventions

judge.evidence_empirical: We address these issues in two preregistered lab experiments (N1 = 191, N2 = 321) and four quasi-experimental in-game surveys implemented in Harmony Square (N3 = 559) and Bad News (N4 = 2,558, N5 = 419, N6 = 882).
judge.evidence_topic: Gamification is a promising approach to reducing misinformation susceptibility. Previous research has found that "inoculation" games such as Bad News and Harmony Square help build cognitive resistance against misinformation.
judge.reason: O achado extraído reflete precisamente a conclusão do resumo: que exercícios de feedback aumentam a discriminação, principalmente melhorando a detecção de notícias reais. O resumo afirma: 'we find that this significantly boosts discernment compared with playing the game without a feedback exercise, primarily by improving accuracy at detecting real news.'
